Data: mat22 s3.p39#4 links s3.p36#1.

instances: gre23 claims over the 120/160 °C pair (the cycled temperature has no single value); yim20 process pressure in hPa; every fact of a process-defining or filter quantity now converts to that quantity's unit (units outside UNIT_BASE, e.g. m2/g or cm2 V-1 s-1, sit on quantities never converted)

observed: One word, 'computed', marked two different things: a value the authors calculated and printed in the paper, and a value this layer derives from other facts (lists.DERIVED), with its inputs and assumed facts; a reader could not tell gre23's printed 17000 Torr-s from yim20's exposure derived from an assumed pressure.
root_cause: query.kind gave paper facts of type derived (data_kind calculated or fit) and calculated settings the kind 'computed', and derived_record gave this layer's values the same kind; every check on 'computed' then treated the authors' values as this layer's (their non-default definition hidden on the page, their ± dropped from reproducibility).
instances: facts computed by the authors: 145 (yim20 108, mat22 4, gre23 33: derived facts with data_kind calculated or fit, 2 gre23 settings, 1 gre23 claim); on experiment and input rows 142 records computed by the authors (yim20 99, mat22 4, gre23 39) and 299 computed here (yim20 171, mat22 99, gre23 29); every check on the kind: query.compare's definition note, query.ctext, report.lite (definition and formula), the page's preference of a stated over a derived value, questions.py KW, Q11 and Q25
fix: query.kind returns 'computed by the authors'; derived_record and ctext 'computed here'; lists.KIND_WORDS has both words; each check on the old kind now names 'computed here' (a derived value: its formula is its definition, it ranks after a stated value), so the authors' values keep their definition and uncertainty
verified: verified: the 145 facts give 'computed by the authors', every derived record 'computed here'; answers change only in the word except Q16 (the authors' XRD wt% now shows its unstated basis, P4) and Q25 (gre23's GPC spread between pieces, an authors' value, now listed); check passes; the 26 answered through query.py; the page's acceptance unchanged

observed: Found in the smoke test: the Knowledge base answer said the paper corrects sample 14 for its pillar layout; the correction is this layer's (query.detail's confounder correction), and the tool line gave it no kind.
root_cause: Since P34 a value record says 'computed here', but the tool lines for what query.py computes outside value records (effect against noise, power-law fits, confounder corrections, a two-item ratio or difference, a claim's scope) carried no kind, so a model could take them for the authors' work.
instances: all 21 comparisons: 90 effect judgements, 30 fits, 14 confounder corrections (yim20 series); every two-item ratio or difference of compare; the scope of all 187 claims; derived values already carried 'computed here' (P34)
fix: ask.py tool lines: 'effect on … (kind: computed here)', 'fit (kind: computed here)', 'correction (kind: computed here)', '… ratio/difference … (kind: computed here)', 'scope (kind: computed here)'; tool descriptions say these are computed here, not by the authors. query.py unchanged
verified: verified: detail(yim20:cmp:E) labels its 9 effects, 7 fits and their corrections; compare labels its ratios; claims label their scope; check passes; the 26 answered (no answer changes: the tool layer only)

fix: facts scripts: quantity and qualifiers on those 31 definitions (yim20 SYM_Q for the nomenclature); ask.py: a result line in find, detail and compare carries ' · defined as: "<up to 90 characters>" [id]', the most specific definition of the paper whose qualifiers the result key carries; source(id) gives it in full
verified: verified: yim20 PD50 rows carry fig3.cap#1, S_I and S_II rows tabu2.r19c0#1 and r20c0#1, gre23 Δn_g and ȳ rows s12.p9#1 and #3; check passes; the 26 answered with no answer changed

observed: Answers ran long: the SHARED prompt asked to say what the sources do not cover and to state every assumption, and gave no length, so answers listed every related value and repeated conditions in sentences.

No max_tokens enforcement (reasoning tokens count against it); Anthropic's MAX_TOKENS stays a cost guard. ask.words counts the answer's words (markers, table rules and lone punctuation excluded); each record holds words and check_line starts with it

observed: A wrong answer could not be traced: the records held each tool call's name, arguments and sizes, but not the text the tool returned.

observed: Earlier runs: models sent arguments the tools silently ignored (a misspelled argument, a value that matched nothing) and got back an unfiltered or empty result, spending calls before they found the right names.
root_cause: run_tool read only the arguments it knew and passed the rest to query.py unchecked; a filter that matched nothing returned 'no results'; compare took an abscissa x that shaped a plot the tool never prints.
instances: every tool and argument: unknown argument names, wrong types (string, integer, number, boolean, array, object), values outside an enum (paper, material, structure, quantity, parts, author), ids that name nothing (detail, source, compare, claims.linked), variables that are no quantity or mechanism, missing required arguments, filters that match nothing; compare.x
fix: tools.validate checks each call against its JSON schema, then the ids and variables against the data; an error names the valid arguments, or the valid or nearest values, or says the id names nothing; a call that matches nothing returns an error naming its filters; null counts as not given; every object schema declares additionalProperties false (the Google adapter drops the keyword, the tool layer still rejects); compare.x removed
verified: verified with 25 probes (every pattern on every tool, and valid calls still answered); no model call

observed: There was no way in by words: a researcher's term had to be guessed as a tool's argument token, one at a time.
root_cause: The tools filtered by controlled ids only (paper, quantity, id); no tool read the text of the records.
instances: every record of the three papers: 2288 (method notes 584, settings 474, values 465, claims 185, cited values 144, definitions 96, process notes 93, experiments 86, cited works 62, notes 51, comparison sets 21, model runs 11, uncertainties 10, inputs 6)
fix: query.search_records and query.search: a lexical BM25 search over each record's statement, label, quantity name, qualifiers, method and mentions; tokens lowercased, _ and - as spaces, plurals folded, numbers and units kept; no embeddings, no synonym list. Tool search(words, paper?, offset?): ranked lines '[id] record type · line' (at most 200 characters, 25 per page); values and settings collapse to one line per paper and quantity with their distinct values, identical lines show once with their count. The page: one search box in the filter line, results in the left list, the same tokens and weights (report.py ships them), a result opens its detail or source panel; the filter line keeps one line at 1280 px (labels folded into the selects)
verified: verified: the page's top 8 equal query.search's for three probes; empty and unmatched words return errors; check passes; the page checks pass

observed: The model did not know the knowledge base's names: it guessed quantity and setting tokens one by one.
root_cause: The descriptions listed quantity ids from lists.py (including ones no paper holds) without the plain names the data use or where they occur.
instances: all 81 result names and 83 setting names of the three papers' experiments, and the 14 record types of search
fix: query.vocabulary: every result and setting name generated from the data at startup, with the papers it occurs in and how many experiments have it; tools.vocabulary_text puts it, with the record types and their counts, into the descriptions of search (and of values, P42), names only above about 3,000 tokens (now about 1,240); it grows with the corpus
verified: verified: the search description carries the vocabulary (about 1,400 tokens in all); each of the 164 names finds at least one record by search; no model call
